title: Advanced IV Estimation with ivreg2r
text: vignette covers features ivreg2r beyond basic two-stage least squares workflow vignette("introduction"): alternative estimators, instrument-validity tests, weak-instrument-robust inference, two-way clustering, reduced form. organized around canonical example groups — Mroz labor-supply equation carries help file’s testing arc, Griliches wage equation help file’s orthogonality example Baum, Schaffer & Stillman’s (2007) weak-instrument redundancy illustrations, Klein’s consumption function separates estimators — adds two-way clustered IV example cigarette-demand panel. topics : LIML, Fuller, k-class estimation, including canonical Klein consumption function Instrument-validity tests: overidentification, orthogonality C-statistic, endogeneity, redundancy Weak-instrument-robust inference (Anderson-Rubin Stock-Wright statistics) Two-way clustering, including instrumental variables Reduced-form regression degrees--freedom adjustments HAC AC standard errors, l()/d() time-series operators, GMM continuously-updated estimator, panel variance estimators (Kiefer, Driscoll-Kraay, cluster-plus-kernel), partialling regressors, user-supplied weighting matrices, see vignette("time-series-gmm"). four weight types documented vignette("introduction") ?ivreg2. Five bundled datasets appear : Mroz (1987) female labor-supply data (mroz), Klein’s (1950) Model macroeconomic series (klein), Griliches (1976) young-men’s wage data (griliches), NLS young-women panel (nlswork, distributed Stata’s [XT] manual), Baltagi cigarette-demand panel (cigar).
code: library(ivreg2r) data(mroz) data(klein) data(griliches) data(nlswork)

title: Advanced IV Estimation with ivreg2r
text: Mroz (1987) dataset contains 753 married women 1975 Panel Study Income Dynamics, 428 working (inlf == 1) observed wages. Years education (educ) potentially endogenous wage equation ability bias. Following illustrative specification used throughout Stata’s ivreg2 help file Baum, Schaffer & Stillman (2007, pp. 471–472), excluded instruments age numbers children home 6 (kidslt6) 6–18 (kidsge6). exclusion restrictions illustrative contestable — children plausibly affect wage offers labor-supply channels — help file adopts precisely make instrument-testing machinery interesting. baseline regresses log wages experience square, education instrumented three excluded instruments. Three excluded instruments one endogenous regressor leave two overidentifying restrictions, makes model useful comparing estimators testing instruments:

title: Advanced IV Estimation with ivreg2r
text: Fuller’s (1977) modified LIML uses k = lambda - alpha / (N - L), L number instruments including exogenous regressors alpha Fuller parameter. standard choice fuller = 1 recommended Fuller (1977) Davidson & MacKinnon (1993, pp. 649–650), cited Baum, Schaffer & Stillman (2007, p. 479):
code: fit_fuller1 <- ivreg2(lwage ~ exper + expersq | educ | age + kidslt6 + kidsge6,                       data = mroz_work, fuller = 1) c(k = fit_fuller1$kclass_value, educ = unname(coef(fit_fuller1)["educ"])) #>          k       educ  #> 0.99927193 0.09666366

title: Advanced IV Estimation with ivreg2r
text: k-class family nests OLS (k = 0), 2SLS (k = 1), LIML (k = lambda). kclass argument accepts arbitrary k; documented non-trivial choice Nagar’s (1959) bias-adjusted estimator k = 1 + (L - K) / N, L - K number overidentifying restrictions. Rather hand-counting L K, derive fitted baseline — rankzz rank full instrument matrix rank number estimated coefficients: Fuller Nagar estimators tend better finite-sample behavior 2SLS weak instruments, though neither robust violations ..d. assumption (Baum, Schaffer & Stillman, 2007, pp. 478–479).
code: N <- nobs(fit_2sls) L <- fit_2sls$rankzz K <- fit_2sls$rank k_nagar <- 1 + (L - K) / N fit_nagar <- ivreg2(lwage ~ exper + expersq | educ | age + kidslt6 + kidsge6,                     data = mroz_work, kclass = k_nagar) c(L = L, K = K, k = k_nagar, educ = unname(coef(fit_nagar)["educ"])) #>          L          K          k       educ  #> 6.00000000 4.00000000 1.00467290 0.09436094

title: Advanced IV Estimation with ivreg2r

Setting coviv = TRUE computes covariance 2SLS projection (k = 1) instead, keeping LIML residuals meat. ..d. errors, LIML COVIV coincides continuously-updated estimator — demonstration appears Klein suite : asserted identity makes division labor explicit: COVIV changes covariance, coefficients exactly LIML coefficients, displayed standard error comes 2SLS-bread sandwich.

title: Advanced IV Estimation with ivreg2r
text: tests follow escalating order help file’s testing examples: joint overidentification test, test subset instruments (help file’s Griliches example), test single regressor’s endogeneity, empty-endogenous form included regressor, finally LIML overidentification statistics. code: fit_full <- ivreg2(   lw ~ s + expr + tenure + rns + smsa + factor(year) | iq | med + kww + age,   data = griliches, small = TRUE )  # Partial the year dummies out of every variable by hand yd <- model.matrix(~ factor(year), data = griliches) resid_on_years <- function(v) lm.fit(yd, v)$residuals gril_fwl <- data.frame(lapply(   griliches[c("lw", "s", "expr", "tenure", "rns", "smsa",               "iq", "med", "kww", "age")],   resid_on_years ))  fit_fwl <- ivreg2(   lw ~ 0 + s + expr + tenure + rns + smsa | iq | med + kww + age,   data = gril_fwl, small = TRUE, sdofminus = 7 )  shared <- names(coef(fit_fwl)) max(abs(coef(fit_full)[shared] - coef(fit_fwl)[shared])) #> [1] 3.330669e-16 max(abs(sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_full)))[shared] - sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_fwl)))[shared])) #> [1] 3.469447e-18 c(sigma_full = fit_full$sigma, sigma_fwl = fit_fwl$sigma) #> sigma_full  sigma_fwl  #>  0.3266951  0.3266951 demean_gm <- function(v, g) v - ave(v, g) + mean(v) gril_within <- data.frame(lapply(   griliches[c("lw", "s", "expr", "tenure")],   demean_gm, g = griliches$year )) G <- length(unique(griliches$year))  fit_lsdv <- ivreg2(lw ~ s + expr + tenure + factor(year),                    data = griliches, small = TRUE) fit_fe <- ivreg2(lw ~ s + expr + tenure, data = gril_within,                  small = TRUE, dofminus = G - 1)  slopes <- c("s", "expr", "tenure") max(abs(coef(fit_lsdv)[slopes] - coef(fit_fe)[slopes])) #> [1] 2.081668e-17 max(abs(sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_lsdv)))[slopes] - sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_fe)))[slopes])) #> [1] 2.602085e-18 c(sigma_lsdv = fit_lsdv$sigma, sigma_fe = fit_fe$sigma,   df_lsdv = fit_lsdv$df.residual, df_fe = fit_fe$df.residual) #> sigma_lsdv   sigma_fe    df_lsdv      df_fe  #>   0.337452   0.337452 748.000000 748.000000

First 2SLS baseline, two-step GMM: first step estimates model 2SLS forms optimal weighting matrix residuals; second step re-estimates weighting, Hansen (1982) J statistic tests overidentifying restrictions. Following published narrative, ..d. 2SLS estimate unemployment coefficient -0.155 clearly significant, HAC-GMM estimate falls -0.100 (p = 0.114): serial correlation accounted , apparent significance disappears. continuously-updated estimator (CUE) completes arc. CUE jointly optimizes GMM objective parameter vector weighting matrix, GMM generalization LIML non-..d. errors. Continuing equation: CUE moves coefficient direction, -0.048 (p = 0.454), Hansen J 2.793 (p = 0.425) leaving overidentifying restrictions comfortably unrejected. Like LIML, CUE finite moments order regardless degree overidentification, finite-sample distribution can heavy tails (Hansen, Heaton & Yaron 1996). objective can multiple local optima, Baum, Schaffer & Stillman (2007, p. 479) warn CUE estimation can slow problematic number parameters substantial. ivreg2r uses BFGS optimization Nelder-Mead refinement, starting 2SLS estimates ..d. weighting two-step GMM estimates robust, cluster, kernel variance, matching Stata’s documented behavior. ill-conditioned models objective can possess economically degenerate minima negative R-squared, documented property CUE (Hausman, Lewis, Menzel & Newey 2011); , Stata ivreg2r converge degenerate solution, inspect J statistic R-squared trusting CUE fit.

title: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation with Diagnostics

title: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation with Diagnostics
text: Estimators: OLS, 2SLS, LIML, Fuller, k-class, two-step efficient GMM, CUE Standard errors: classical, robust, one- two-way clustering, HAC/AC (8 kernels), Kiefer, Driscoll-Kraay, cluster+kernel Diagnostics: weak identification (Kleibergen-Paap rk, Cragg-Donald, Stock-Yogo critical values), underidentification, overidentification (Sargan, Hansen J), endogeneity, first-stage F/partial R-squared, Anderson-Rubin, Stock-Wright S, orthogonality, redundancy Integration: tidy(), glance(), augment() via broom estimators diagnostics tested Stata ivreg2 benchmarks.

title: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation — ivreg2
text: formula formula: y ~ exog (OLS), y ~ exog | endo | instruments (IV), y ~ exog | 0 | instruments (endogenous regressors, excluded instruments contributing surplus moment conditions — Stata's (=z1 z2) form). latter estimated OLS; surplus conditions drive Sargan/Hansen J overidentification test orthog C-tests, method = "gmm2s" vcov = "robust" gives Cragg's (1983) heteroskedastic OLS (HOLS) estimator (default iid VCE two-step weighting matrix proportional \((Z'Z)^{-1}\) estimates equal OLS exactly). data data frame containing variables formula. weights Optional analytic weights expression (evaluated data), equivalent Stata's [aw=varname]. Must strictly positive. aweights pweights, weights normalized internally sum N, following Stata's convention. makes sigma (RMSE) scale-invariant types: multiplying weights constant changes coefficients, standard errors, test statistics. Frequency importance weights normalized — redefine N sum(weights) (see weight_type), scale matters construction. Note: aweights pweights, sigma differ lm()(..., weights = w) factor sqrt(N / sum(w)) lm() uses raw (unnormalized) weights. Coefficients identical lm() OLS; SEs VCV matrix additionally match lm() small = TRUE (default small = FALSE reports Stata-convention SEs without N - K finite-sample correction). subset Optional subset expression (evaluated data). na.action Function handling NAs (default na.omit). Use na.exclude drop incomplete cases estimation reinsert NAs omitted positions fitted(), residuals(), predict() output, results align original data frame. Stata drops missing observations silently (equivalent na.omit) analogue na.exclude. vcov Character: covariance type. One "iid" (classical), "robust" (White heteroskedasticity-robust), "HAC" (heteroskedasticity autocorrelation consistent), "AC" (autocorrelation consistent). Use small = TRUE apply finite-sample corrections. match Stata's ivreg2, robust: use vcov = "robust". match Stata's ivreg2, robust small: use vcov = "robust", small = TRUE. clusters One-sided formula specifying one two cluster variables (e.g. ~ firmid one-way, ~ firmid + year two-way). Two-way clustering uses Cameron-Gelbach-Miller (2006) formula. effective cluster count min(M1, M2) per Stata convention. small argument controls whether finite-sample correction (N-1)/(N-K) * M/(M-1) applied (matching Stata's cluster() small combination). endog Character vector endogenous regressor names test exogeneity (endogeneity test / C-statistic). NULL (default), tests endogenous regressors. Names must match variables endogenous part formula. Ignored OLS models. Note: Unlike Stata's ivreg2, computes endogeneity test endog() option explicitly specified, ivreg2r computes automatically IV models. orthog Character vector instrument names test orthogonality (instrument-subset C-statistic). Names must included excluded instruments (endogenous regressors intercept). NULL (default), orthogonality test computed. Ignored OLS models. Equivalent Stata's orthog() option. redundant Character vector excluded instrument names test redundancy (zero first-stage explanatory power). test KP rk LM test H0: rank=0 first-stage coefficient matrix tested instruments, conditional maintained instruments. NULL (default), redundancy test computed. Ignored OLS models. Equivalent Stata's redundant() option. method Character: estimation method. One "2sls" (default), "liml", "kclass", "gmm2s" (two-step efficient GMM), "cue" (continuously updated GMM estimator). OLS models (1-part formula), ignored. fuller > 0 specified, method automatically promoted "liml". "gmm2s" uses inverse moment covariance matrix optimal weighting matrix, yielding efficient estimates specified error structure. Incompatible fuller kclass. "cue" continuously updates moment conditions moment covariance candidate beta optimization. iid errors (robust/cluster/kernel VCE), CUE options equivalent LIML coviv = TRUE. non-iid errors, CUE generalizes LIML produce efficient estimates. Incompatible fuller, kclass, wmatrix, smatrix. CUE optimizer note: package uses R's optim() (BFGS + Nelder-Mead, scaled starting values) Stata uses Mata's optimize() (modified Newton-Raphson). CUE objective non-convex can multiple local minima, can possess economically degenerate minima (e.g., negative R-squared) – documented property CUE ratio objective (Hausman, Lewis, Menzel & Newey, 2011), optimizer failure. every benchmarked model two implementations agree minimum, including one pathological case, converge degenerate basin; basins extremely flat, coefficient agreement across implementations limited digits. Inspect J-statistic R-squared judge whether CUE solution economically sensible. kclass Numeric scalar: user-supplied k value k-class estimation. supplied, method automatically set "kclass". Must non-negative. combined method = "liml" fuller. fuller Numeric scalar: Fuller (1977) modification parameter. Must positive. supplied, method automatically set "liml" k = lambda - fuller / (N - L). fuller = 1 gives bias-corrected LIML estimator; fuller = 4 targets MSE. combined kclass. coviv Logical: TRUE, use 2SLS bread (X_hat'X_hat)^{-1} instead k-class bread VCV computation LIML/k-class estimation. gives "COVIV" (covariance IV estimates) VCV robust misspecification LIML model. Silently ignored OLS 2SLS. Default FALSE. small Logical: TRUE, use small-sample corrections (t/F instead z/chi-squared, N-K denominator sigma). dofminus Non-negative integer: large-sample degrees--freedom adjustment. Subtracted N large-sample variance formulas (e.g., sigma = rss/(N-dofminus)). Useful fixed effects partialled . Equivalent Stata's dofminus() option. sdofminus Non-negative integer: small-sample degrees--freedom adjustment. Restricted IID VCE — incompatible robust, cluster, HAC, GMM estimation. kernel Character: kernel function HAC/AC standard errors. One "bartlett", "parzen", "truncated", "tukey-hanning", "tukey-hamming", "qs" (quadratic spectral), "daniell", "tent". specified without explicit vcov change, vcov automatically set: "iid" becomes "AC", "robust" becomes "HAC". Requires bw tvar. Must positive numeric, "auto" automatic selection via Newey-West (1994). Auto selection available Bartlett, Parzen, Quadratic Spectral kernels , supported panel data (ivar). Lags resolved time value (gap-aware), mirroring Stata's tsset. ivar Character: name panel identifier variable data. Optional; needed panel data (HAC/AC estimation, time-series operators lag within panel units). kiefer Logical: TRUE, use Kiefer (1980) VCE — autocorrelation-consistent kernel = Truncated bandwidth = T (full time span). Requires panel data (tvar + ivar). Incompatible robust VCE, clustering, explicit kernel bandwidth. Equivalent Stata's ivreg2 ..., kiefer. dkraay Positive numeric scalar: bandwidth Driscoll-Kraay (1998) VCE. specified, clusters time variable applies kernel smoothing across time lags, producing standard errors robust cross-sectional dependence. Requires panel data (tvar + ivar). Incompatible explicit bw. kernel specified, defaults Bartlett. Equivalent Stata's ivreg2 ..., dkraay(3). wmatrix Numeric matrix: user-supplied L x L weighting matrix GMM estimation, L number instruments (including exogenous regressors). supplied without method = "gmm2s", produces inefficient GMM full sandwich VCV (method becomes "gmmw"). combined method = "gmm2s", used first-step weighting matrix (second step uses optimal weighting matrix). Must symmetric. Incompatible method = "liml", kclass, fuller. method "gmm2s", ignored without robust VCE, clustering, HAC (warning). Equivalent Stata's wmatrix() option. used (ignored), echoed back fit$W, matching Stata's e(W). matrix dimnames matched instrument columns name (reordered needed, mirroring Stata's matsort; names cover instrument list error); unnamed matrix used positionally, instrument column order. smatrix Numeric matrix: user-supplied L x L moment covariance matrix GMM estimation. supplied, GMM estimation uses matrix instead computing Omega residuals. Implies efficient GMM (method promoted "gmm2s" "2sls"). Must symmetric. Incompatible method = "liml", kclass, fuller. Equivalent Stata's smatrix() option. Echoed back fit$S (never recomputed), matching Stata's e(S). matrix dimnames matched instrument columns name (reordered needed, mirroring Stata's matsort); unnamed matrix used positionally, instrument column order. b0 Numeric vector: evaluate CUE objective fixed parameter vector without optimization. supplied, method promoted "cue" J(b0) statistic computed stored. Identification diagnostics (underid, weak-id, first-stage, AR, SW, endogeneity, orthog) suppressed (matching Stata's b0() option). Length must equal number regressors K. Named vectors reordered match model matrix columns; unnamed vectors used -model matrix column order. Incompatible method = "gmm2s", "liml", kclass, fuller, wmatrix. noid Logical: TRUE, suppress computation underidentification, weak identification, redundancy test statistics. Overidentification, Anderson-Rubin, Stock-Wright, endogeneity, first-stage diagnostics still computed. Default FALSE. Useful speeding simulation loops rank-based identification tests expensive. NULL (default): partialling. default, sdofminus automatically incremented number partialled variables (including constant). Use nopartialsmall = TRUE suppress adjustment. Default FALSE. Equivalent Stata's nopartialsmall option. center Logical: TRUE, subtract mean moment conditions (scores) computing S matrix (meat sandwich VCE). Default FALSE. Centering affects non-homoskedastic VCE types (HC, cluster, HAC); warning issued used IID AC VCE. However, endogeneity test (endog) computes S matrix restricted model without centering, even center = TRUE. matches Stata's ivreg2, center forwarded recursive call endogeneity test. psd Character NULL: PSD correction moment covariance matrix S. title: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation — ivreg2
text: object class "ivreg2". Beyond usual components (coefficients, residuals, vcov, diagnostics, ...), object stores estimated moment-condition covariance matrix $S GMM weighting matrix $W, corresponding Stata's e(S) e(W): $S present every fit. Normalization matches Stata's m_omega: iid sigma^2 (Z'Z)/N sigma^2 = RSS/(N - dofminus); robust HAC, meat divided N - dofminus; cluster, meat divided N; psd-corrected psd set; built centered moments center = TRUE. user-supplied smatrix echoed, never recomputed never psd-corrected. $W NULL method = "liml" "kclass" (Stata, weighting matrix defined k-class estimators). two-step GMM, CUE, b0 fits inverse defining $S; one-step OLS/2SLS (1/sigma^2) (Z'Z/N)^{-1}; user-supplied wmatrix echoed (first-step weighting matrix method = "gmm2s"). Rows columns named R instrument columns — (Intercept) rather Stata's _cons, R column order (exogenous regressors excluded instruments) rather Stata's. Passing fit$S back via smatrix reproduces corresponding efficient-GMM fit, mirroring e(S) reuse workflow Stata's ivreg2 help file.

title: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation — ivreg2
text: model carries instruments regressors, ivreg2() automatically reports overidentification test: Sargan (1958) statistic vcov = "iid", Hansen J statistic robust, cluster, HAC errors. test evaluates L - K overidentifying restrictions jointly, L number instruments K number regressors. rejection indicates least one instrument violates orthogonality condition, without identifying one. non-rejection necessary sufficient instrument validity. test power bias shared every instrument, orthogonality conditions fail direction can still appear jointly satisfied. test also uninformative K exactly-identifying moment conditions, whose validity must defended substantive grounds. exactly identified model overidentifying restrictions, therefore overidentification test. endogeneity test, also called C-statistic difference test, asks whether regressors treated endogenous instead treated exogenous. overidentification statistic model adds suspect regressors instrument set, treating exogenous, minus model treats endogenous. null exogeneity, difference follows chi-square distribution degrees freedom equal number regressors tested. overidentification statistics formed estimated moment covariance, guarantees difference non-negative (Hayashi 2000). ivreg2() computes test automatically every IV model, whereas Stata computes endog() option given explicitly. endog argument selects endogenous regressors tested. statistic takes difference--Sargan form iid errors difference--Hansen-J form robust, cluster, HAC errors.

title: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation — ivreg2
text: LIML, Fuller's modification, general k-class estimators alternatives 2SLS motivated weak instruments. LIML approximately median-unbiased, Stock-Yogo weak-identification thresholds forgiving 2SLS. LIML finite-sample moments order, however. sampling distribution can therefore dispersed, individual estimates can lie far truth. Fuller's (1977) modification sets k = lambda - fuller / (N - L), yields estimator finite moments. choice fuller = 1 approximately best-unbiased, fuller = 4 minimizes mean squared error, within standard weak-instrument framework. Weak-identification pretesting LIML Fuller uses estimator-specific critical values rather 2SLS values. LIML coincides 2SLS model exactly identified, LIML eigenvalue equals one case. what: ivreg2r: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation with Diagnostics — ivreg2r-package
title: ivreg2r: Extended Instrumental Variables Estimation with Diagnostics — ivreg2r-package
text: Comprehensive instrumental variables GMM estimation automatic diagnostics, inspired Stata's 'ivreg2' (Baum, Schaffer & Stillman). Supports 2SLS, LIML, Fuller, k-class, two-step efficient GMM, continuously-updated (CUE) estimators. Provides classical, robust, cluster-robust, HAC, Driscoll-Kraay standard errors. Reports weak identification, underidentification, overidentification, endogeneity tests estimation time. outputs verified Stata within tight numerical tolerances.

title: Time-series operators for ivreg2 formulas — ts-operators
Time-series operators for ivreg2 formulas — ts-operators
text: x numeric variable model data. k Lag order(s) l(); difference order(s) d(). Non-negative integer (vector allowed, expanded one term per element).

title: Time-series operators for ivreg2 formulas — ts-operators
text: used inside ivreg2() formula: numeric vector aligned model data. Calling functions anywhere else error.

title: Time-series operators for ivreg2 formulas — ts-operators
text: Lags computed time value, row position: l(x, k) time t value x time t - k within panel unit. observation exists t - k (start series, gap time variable), lag NA row dropped estimation sample — exactly Stata's behavior. Lags never cross panel-unit boundaries. data need sorted.

title: Time-series operators for ivreg2 formulas — ts-operators
text: Following Stata (fixest), d(x, k) k-th order (iterated) difference (1-L)^k x, matching Stata's Dk.x; fixest's d(x, k) distance-k difference x - l(x, k). two agree k = 1.

title: Time-series operators for ivreg2 formulas — ts-operators
text: Operators require tvar (ivar panel data) passed ivreg2(); l() d() standalone lag utilities signal error called outside ivreg2() formula (use, e.g., dplyr::lag() consecutive-periods check, fixest/collapse/ plm, general-purpose panel lagging). time variable must integer-valued (greater \(-2^{53}\), \(2^{53}\)), like Stata's tsset — lag arithmetic fractional astronomically large time values exact floating point. lag/difference order k must constant non-negative integer (integer vector ranges); leads (negative k), nested operators (l(d(x))), ranges left-hand side (model single dependent variable) supported. operators appear among regressors, predict(fit, newdata) recomputes within newdata, newdata must contain history rows needed lags; rows whose lags missing get NA predictions (matching Stata). Operators confined instrument part impose requirement newdata.

title: ivreg2r 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN release. ivreg2r provides extended instrumental variables GMM estimation automatic diagnostics, inspired Stata’s ivreg2 (Baum, Schaffer & Stillman). Estimators: 2SLS, LIML, Fuller, k-class, two-step efficient GMM, continuously-updated estimator (CUE). Variance estimators: classical, heteroskedasticity-robust, one- two-way cluster-robust, HAC/AC eight kernels automatic bandwidth selection, Kiefer, Driscoll-Kraay. Diagnostics reported estimation time: weak identification (Kleibergen-Paap, Cragg-Donald, Stock-Yogo critical values), underidentification, overidentification (Sargan, Hansen J, Stock-Wright S), first-stage tests (Sanderson-Windmeijer, Angrist-Pischke), endogeneity, orthogonality. Tidyverse integration: three-part formula interface tidy(), glance(), augment() methods. Bundled datasets used throughout help-file examples vignettes: card, mroz, wagepan, griliches, klein, grunfeld, abdata, nlswork, phillips, stockwatson, cigar. outputs verified Stata ivreg2 within tight numerical tolerances.
